place: Wexham: the Rook orchard
scene: Tamsin walks the disputed boundary with Orla and Bryony, who speak to each other only through her. Orla has a buyer and a date; Bryony has the trees. The roll's line runs through the middle of the old pear row, which neither sister believes. Tamsin takes the job at her day rate and says she will have an answer by the new year
what_changes: Tamsin is hired; the boundary is a question on the roll, not just between sisters; Orla's sale has a deadline
reader_knows_by_end: Two sisters fighting over an orchard; the boundary on the roll is odd; Tamsin is a title researcher who used to be at the Calloway registry; she needs the fee
pov_lens: Notices boundary stones, the sisters' hands, which of them owns the boots by the door; misreads the quarrel as about money; hides that she needs the fee and that she left the registry under a cloud

place: Calloway: Tamsin and Juno's house
scene: Evening. Juno is at the piano working out her anniversary setting of the Naming Day hymn and wants Tamsin to hear the last verse. Fen Archer's first anniversary column ("Senna for our times") is on the table. Juno asks, again, whether they are going to have a child; Tamsin says after this job
what_changes: Juno's question is put off once too often, and Juno lets it go in a way Tamsin does not notice
reader_knows_by_end: Calloway's story of Senna: the registrar who died for the rolls in 647, the 375th anniversary coming, the Cause; the hymn and its last line; Juno's question
pov_lens: Notices Fen's mistakes of fact and the pencil marks on Juno's score; misreads Juno's question as a question about timing; hides that the orchard job pays less than she told Juno

place: Calloway: the Registry search room and the Registry Chapel
scene: Tamsin pulls the Wexham rolls for the orchard. To reach the search room she walks through the Registry Chapel, past the relic rolls in their cases and a page of the old alms book open beside them, as she did every working day for fifteen years. Agnes Mure stops her in the corridor: her search access is a courtesy, and the anniversary is not a time for freelancers making work
what_changes: Tamsin finds that the orchard's line was among the entries corrected in Senna's own rolls; Agnes puts a condition on her access
reader_knows_by_end: The relic rolls and the hooked correction stroke on them; the chapel alms book (Jory of the porch, bread and a blanket) as one exhibit among many; Tamsin's falling-out with Agnes; the orchard line is in Senna's corrected rolls
pov_lens: Notices the stroke without looking at it, the way one notices a clock; misreads Agnes's warning as spite; hides from Agnes that she still has her old pass

place: Wexham: the meeting house, then the Rook kitchen
scene: Bryony reads at the Plain Keeping meeting house: one of The Schoolmistress's Letters, about a child who makes her capitals backwards. At home she takes the family box down from the dresser, finds the letter that describes the orchard, and decides to give the letters to Tamsin rather than let Orla's solicitor near them
what_changes: Bryony decides to use the letters to win, and to keep them out of Orla's hands
reader_knows_by_end: The meeting house reads a teacher's letters as devotion; the Rooks have an old family box; Bryony knows something about the letters she is not saying
pov_lens: Notices the weather, the dresser, Orla's car not in the lane; misreads giving the letters to a stranger as keeping them private; hides that she knows the meeting-house letters are "Grandmother Senna's"

place: Wexham: the Rook kitchen
scene: Bryony puts the bundle on the kitchen table. Letters signed "Senna", dated 647 to 677. The one that settles the boundary is dated 668, and its line matches the old pear row, not Senna's corrected roll. In its margin is the hooked stroke. One letter is in another hand, signed M.; Tamsin sets it aside. She asks to borrow the bundle and Bryony says no, then yes, for a week
what_changes: Tamsin has seen the saint's stroke in a letter written twenty-one years after the saint's death, and has said nothing to Bryony about it
reader_knows_by_end: The letters exist; they are signed Senna and dated after 647; the stroke matches; the boundary in the letter matches the uncorrected line; there is a letter from an M.
pov_lens: Notices the stroke, then the date, then the boundary; misreads the boundary detail as a family mistake; hides her recognition from Bryony

place: Calloway: the Order's chapter house
scene: The first sitting of the Cause in the anniversary year. Hesketh presents; Perpetua, as Examiner, enters her formal doubts, which are the ones she enters every time. Honor Bale rehearses the Great Life's death scene for the sitting, with two lines Perpetua half notices. Councillor Teague is in the gallery; Fen is in the press seats. Afterwards Hesketh and Perpetua argue about evidence over a bad lunch, as they have for thirty years
what_changes: The Cause is formally opened, with a vote set for midsummer; Perpetua notices that Delphine and Hesketh have spoken before
reader_knows_by_end: The Cause's procedure (Advocate, Examiner, vote); the Great Life's death scene as Honor reads it; Hesketh and Perpetua's friendship; Delphine's interest
pov_lens: Notices Honor's phrasing against the printed text, the gallery, Hesketh's tiredness; misreads Delphine's presence as civic duty; hides that she wants the Cause to succeed for Hesketh

place: Calloway: the Registry Chapel, after hours
scene: Tamsin uses her old pass to get into the chapel when the choir is rehearsing. She stands at the relic cases with a photograph of the 668 letter on her phone and compares the strokes. Juno's choir sings the hymn's last verse behind her. Juno sees her and does not stop conducting. The tomb's inscription quotes the translation record: "the grave signed with her hand"
what_changes: Tamsin is sure the hand is the same; she has broken Agnes's condition; she does not tell Juno what she was doing
reader_knows_by_end: The stroke matches; a dead saint was writing twenty-one years after her death; the tomb's inscription
pov_lens: Notices the hook at the bottom of the stroke, the angle, the ink; misreads her certainty as proof; hides from Juno what she was looking at

place: Calloway: Kate's family house
scene: The household Reading on the last night of the year. Aunt Ros reads the Aldous roll, oldest name first, and the room answers "kept". Before the roll Kate reads from Marit's diary, as someone in the family always does: Senna "tired and secret all winter", and, among a run of dye orders, a line about giving spoiled lengths to the woman on the chapel porch. Kate and Aunt Ros have their yearly disagreement about Marit: Ros hears a widow keeping her children's grief small, and has a real case; Kate hears a woman angry with Senna for leaving them, and says love and anger are not exclusive; a cousin says Marit was cross with everybody until she was seventy-eight. The food comes in and the argument is dropped. Near the end of the roll is a name the family took in, a foundling from 1890; Kate explains taking in to Juno. Tamsin's voice catches on Senna's name. Kate asks her to help the Cause
what_changes: Kate asks Tamsin for help and reads her silence as grief for her lapsed faith; Tamsin does not answer; the anniversary year begins
reader_knows_by_end: The Reading; Marit's diary and the line about the copying; a woman on the chapel porch, in passing; taking in; Kate is on the Cause committee and descends from Marit; the family already argues about Marit's grief, without knowing what it was
pov_lens: Notices who answers "kept" and who mouths it, who has not eaten, Tamsin's hands; misreads Tamsin's silence as grief; hides that the committee asked her to recruit Tamsin

place: Calloway: the Registry Chapel porch
scene: Interlude: Jory on the porch, present tense. Cold, the step, the people who step over her, the registrar who brings soup and does not ask her name because she knows it
what_changes: None: an interlude
reader_knows_by_end: A lame woman lives on the chapel porch; a registrar feeds her
pov_lens: Never names Senna; never says where Jory will be buried

place: Calloway: Tamsin and Juno's house
scene: The day after the dead day. Tamsin gave the bundle back to Bryony on the 27th, having photographed the boundary letter with Bryony's leave and every other page without it. At the kitchen table she writes her interim report to both sisters: the roll's line stands unless the letter of 668 is admitted as evidence of an older one, and she has to name the letter as her source. Juno, eating keeping loaf out of duty, reads the Wallgate petition's latest letter in the Courier aloud and asks what has been wrong with her since the Reading. Tamsin, talking about the anniversary instead: "They have a Reading of her, and nobody reads the record." Juno says it is the most registrar thing she has ever heard anyone say
what_changes: The letters are named in a report both sisters will read; Tamsin holds a private set of photographs she was not given; Juno knows something is wrong and is told nothing
reader_knows_by_end: Tamsin has copies of the whole bundle; her report must cite the letter; the music quarrel; Juno's patience is wearing thin
pov_lens: Notices the time-stamps on her photographs, Juno's pencil on the score, the loaf going stale; misreads Juno's teasing as lightness; hides the photographs and what she has seen
pressure: Orla's solicitor wants the report; the Wallgate petition

place: Calloway: the Registry stacks and search room
scene: Tamsin fills in the proper slip for the cancelled Wexham roll of 644, the volume Senna's copies replaced, kept since 649 in a locked press as a struck book. A young clerk fetches it and mentions, cheerfully, that Agnes reads every request slip now. On the cancelled page the line between the Rook parcels runs along the eastern edge of the pear row: the line in the letter of 668, and the line the Rook family has always believed. Nobody outside the Registry has been able to see that page since 649. Then she looks again at her photograph of the fourth chapel case from I-07, the original eastern roll, and at Senna's correction on the Rook line, which the facsimile in I-03 left as a grey bar: under the strike, faint but readable in the original, is "eastern edge"
what_changes: The letter of 668 was written by someone who knew the roll before the correction; Agnes knows what Tamsin is looking at
reader_knows_by_end: The letter describes the forged line, not the relic's; whoever wrote it had seen the roll before 646; the Rooks' family boundary is the forged one
pov_lens: Notices the struck volume's binding, the cancelling marks across each page (not Senna's), the clerk's chipped varnish; misreads the clerk's chatter as gossip; hides why the orchard matters

place: Calloway: the Infirmary canteen, then the chapter house
scene: Kate comes off a night shift and meets Juno for the canteen breakfast before Juno's school day. They compare notes on Tamsin, who has told neither of them anything; Juno thinks it is the job, Kate thinks it is the faith. In the evening, at the Cause's lay committee, the anniversary order of service goes round in proof, with its response "Senna Aldous, for the rolls"; the committee argues only about the typeface. Hesketh's secretary thanks Kate warmly for securing Tamsin's help. Kate does not correct her
what_changes: Kate has let the committee believe Tamsin will help; Kate and Juno agree something is wrong and disagree about what
reader_knows_by_end: The liturgy's response "for the rolls"; Kate and Juno's friendship; Kate's standing on the committee and her life on the ward
pov_lens: Notices that Juno has not eaten, the committee's wet coats, a misprint in the proof; misreads Juno's worry as worry about the child; hides that she has promised Tamsin to the committee

place: Wexham: the school record room above the primary school
scene: Tamsin tells the sisters she is checking the school's old boundary maps, and goes to Wexham to follow the letters' writer instead. Win Corley, in a cold room above the primary school, brings out the register of teachers: "Senna, from Calloway, to teach letters", spring 647, no papers noted, Lise Rook her surety. Win sees nothing odd in it: Wexham never asked for papers. She is more interested in the damp, and in showing Tamsin the Return Day ledgers. Tamsin catches the seven o'clock bus with a minute to spare
what_changes: A Senna from Calloway arrived in Wexham in the spring of the saint's death; Tamsin has lied to the sisters about why she was there
reader_knows_by_end: The school record; Wexham asked no papers; Lise Rook took her in; Return Day and the 649 judgment as local history nobody connects with anything
pov_lens: Notices the register's ruling, which entries are in a later hand, Win's careful hands; misreads Win's indifference as discretion; hides the photographs on her phone
pressure: Bryony rings: Orla has had the report

place: Wexham: the orchard, then Orla's pharmacy
scene: Bryony is pruning in the frost when a neighbour shows her Fen Archer's Saturday column on her phone: a Wexham family holds letters "that may be in the saint's own hand", from "a source close to the family". She walks into Orla's pharmacy in her boots, for the first time in a year, and they have it out in front of a woman waiting for a prescription. Orla gave Fen the interim report. At home Bryony takes the box down from the dresser and puts it in the cupboard under the stairs, behind the frost burners
what_changes: The letters are public; Bryony blames Tamsin as much as Orla; the sisters have spoken, badly, for the first time since the funeral
reader_knows_by_end: Fen's column; Orla leaked the report; giving Tamsin the letters did not keep them private; the quarrel is older than the orchard
pov_lens: Notices frost on the cut ends, the mud she leaves on the pharmacy floor, Orla's new car; misreads Orla's pleasure in the attention as greed; hides that she kept a tied packet back from the box in December

place: Calloway: the Order library, then the Wednesday lunch
scene: Hesketh brings Fen's column to their Wednesday lunch and asks Perpetua, as Examiner, to put it to rest. Perpetua has already got hold of the photographs Orla sent the Courier and has looked at the stroke for two evenings. Registry hands were taught, she says; a pupil could have learnt it. Hesketh would rather the Rooks had forged the letters to claim descent, and says so. Over pudding Delphine's name comes up: the Order's chapter votes on selling Ferrier Street in June, and Hesketh needs it quiet
what_changes: Two false theories are now held by intelligent women; Perpetua starts on the Registry's training records; she sees that the Cause and the housing vote are tied
reader_knows_by_end: The pupil theory and the Rook forgery theory; the Ferrier Street deal; thirty years of Wednesday lunches
pov_lens: Notices the stroke's angle in a poor photograph, Hesketh's pills beside her plate, who pays; misreads her own pleasure in the problem as professional; hides that she already thinks the hands are very close

place: Calloway: Holm Lane School hall
scene: Hild's Day. Juno's school puts on the children's play of Saint Hild of the Door and Juno plays the piano for it. Tamsin stands at the back with her phone, which has three messages: Bryony will not take her calls; Kate thanks her for agreeing to help the Cause; Agnes's office asks her to ring. A Year Seven Hild dies against a cardboard door with the speech every child in Calloway knows, and half the hall says the last line with her. Tamsin leaves before the bows. Juno sees her go
what_changes: Tamsin has been promised to the Cause without being asked and is avoiding three women; Juno sees her leave
reader_knows_by_end: Hild's legend and her death speech, as everyone knows them; Kate has told the committee; Bryony blames Tamsin
pov_lens: Notices the painted bolts on the cardboard door, which children mouth the words, the parents filming; misreads Kate's message as pressure rather than a mistake; hides from Juno why she is leaving

place: Wexham: the Plain Keeping meeting house
scene: Tamsin takes the 22 to apologise to Bryony and arrives in the middle of the Sunday reading. Bryony is reading, and the letter is one Tamsin has on her phone, about pruning the schoolhouse pear. The reading copy is in an old hand, centuries old. Afterwards, drying cups in the meeting-house kitchen, Tamsin tells Bryony what she thinks: the Senna of the letters is the Senna of the Registry. Bryony says the letters are Grandmother Senna's and always have been, and the woman in Calloway is a story. She does not forgive the column
what_changes: Tamsin is sure the Wexham Senna is the saint; she has said so to Bryony, who does not believe it and has not forgiven her
reader_knows_by_end: The meeting house has read the bundle's letters for three hundred years as The Schoolmistress's Letters; the Rooks call her Grandmother Senna; letters, boundary and school record make one pattern
pov_lens: Notices the bare walls, the age of the reading copy's hand, Bryony's voice reading; misreads Bryony's anger as only about the leak; hides that she photographed the whole bundle

place: Calloway: Kate's flat
scene: The committee has heard that Agnes Mure complained to the Order about a freelancer "making work" with the Wexham letters, and that the freelancer is Tamsin. Tamsin comes round after Kate's last night shift. Kate, too tired to be careful, asks her straight out, and Tamsin tells her some of it: the stroke, the dates, the school record, not the meeting house. Kate asks her to stop until after the anniversary, for the family and for her. Tamsin says she will. Kate knows she will not, and makes her a bacon sandwich anyway
what_changes: Kate has asked Tamsin to stop; Tamsin has promised; Kate knows the saint may have lived
reader_knows_by_end: Agnes has complained to the Order; Kate knows part of it; Tamsin's promise and what it costs the friendship
pov_lens: Notices Tamsin's cold hands, that she keeps her coat on, her own exhaustion; misreads the part she is told as the whole; hides that she half wants Tamsin to be right
pressure: Kate asks Tamsin to stop; Agnes's complaint

place: Calloway: a great house, the streets, the Registry
scene: Interlude: Hanne Rusk, steward, present tense. An errand day: fish, candles, a dispute with a carter, and a folded note from her mistress to be put into the keeper's own hand at the Registry and nobody else's. She waits in a cold anteroom among clerks bent over rolls, is given a reply, and walks home by the river
what_changes: None: an interlude
reader_knows_by_end: A steward carries a note from her household to the keeper of the Registry, by hand, in the autumn of 645
pov_lens: Never names Benedicta, Carrow or Senna; Hanne does not read the note and does not wonder about it

place: Calloway: the Order library reading room
scene: Looking for anything written about Senna by someone who knew her, Tamsin finds in the Order library's catalogue An Account of Senna Aldous, by Dorcas Pryor, 660, one surviving copy, seldom asked for. Perpetua is in the reading room waiting for the same volume. They read it at one table, in a silence that is half rivalry. It is plain and short and never says Senna died: she "was made dead for the rolls, and the house of the Keeping was the poorer". Perpetua calls it restraint. Tamsin says nothing
what_changes: Tamsin has the earliest account of Senna, and it never says she died; she and Perpetua have met
reader_knows_by_end: Dorcas's Account exists, is cautious, and never says Senna died; Dorcas was her friend and later keeper; Perpetua and Tamsin are working the same evidence from opposite ends
pov_lens: Notices the Account's paper and binding, Perpetua's glass, which pages are worn; misreads Perpetua's reading as a test of her; hides why she wants the book

place: Calloway: Perpetua's flat over the library
scene: A week in the Registry's old training records: hands were taught, stroke by stroke, from a copybook, and Perpetua is right about that, and it does not help, because the copybook's correction stroke has no hook. Hesketh climbs the stairs with soup. Perpetua reads her the Great Life's death scene beside the legend of Saint Hild, and they are the same, almost line for line. Hesketh says shared tradition. Perpetua says borrowed. Hesketh washes up badly
what_changes: The Great Life's death is borrowed from Hild; the pupil theory is weakened, not dead; Perpetua has started to doubt the Life, not just the letters
reader_knows_by_end: Registry hands were taught; the hook is personal; the Great Life's death scene is Hild's
pov_lens: Notices the copybook's stroke, Hesketh's breath on the stairs, the soup's lack of salt; misreads Hesketh's breathlessness as the stairs; hides that her knees are worse

place: Calloway: the Registry Chapel
scene: Honor Bale rehearses the death scene for the anniversary with Juno, who needs the timings for the music. Tamsin has come for Juno's car keys and sits at the back with the printed Great Life from the chapel shop. Honor says two lines that are not in it. Afterwards Honor, delighted to be asked anything, says she has always said them; they came to her one year and stayed. Juno, who has heard them every week since September, did not know they were new
what_changes: Tamsin has watched a text grow in front of her, honestly, and sees how the Great Life itself could have grown
reader_knows_by_end: Honor's two lines are her own; texts grow by additions nobody intends to deceive with; Juno and Honor work together
pov_lens: Notices the printed page against Honor's voice, Honor's thumb on the margin, Juno's stopwatch; misreads Honor's charm as vanity; hides from Juno that she has been to Wexham again

place: Wexham: the solicitor's office above the old bank, then the orchard
scene: The sisters' solicitors meet over Tamsin's interim report. Orla's builder has brought her date forward to the end of April. The Order has written to Orla asking whether the letters might be "examined, and possibly acquired", and Orla wants to hear the offer. Bryony says the letters are not for sale and the trees are not for houses, walks out, and comes back for her gloves. That evening Orla turns up at the orchard for the first time since the funeral, and they prune the pear row together in the last light without discussing anything
what_changes: The sale date is the end of April; the Order has made an approach; the sisters have worked side by side for an hour
reader_knows_by_end: Orla needs the money for her daughter's fees; the Order wants the letters; the quarrel is about their mother
pov_lens: Notices the solicitor's carpet, the cut ends, Orla's hands on the loppers; misreads Orla's coming as a softening about the sale; hides the packet she kept back
pressure: The builder's new date; the Order's letter

place: Calloway: Aunt Ros's house
scene: Without telling Kate, Tamsin calls on Aunt Ros, who spent forty years on the city archive's front desk and is pleased to be asked something properly. Ros brings out Marit's diary in the archive's cotton gloves. Tamsin reads the winter of 646: "S. tired and secret all winter", between madder orders and the children's coughs, and sees a winter of nights at the Registry. Ros mentions that Marit's mother's dyeworks stood on the river below the chapel and made the Registry's ink as well as dyeing cloth. She asks Tamsin to stay for tea and to tell Kate she came. Tamsin stays for tea
what_changes: Marit's "tired and secret" was the copying; Tamsin has gone behind Kate's back; she has a reason to look for the dyeworks
reader_knows_by_end: Marit's diary as a voice; a winter's night work; the dyeworks and the ink; Aunt Ros's case for Marit
pov_lens: Notices Marit's hand and paper, Ros's gloves, the photograph of the Reading on the mantelpiece; misreads Ros's welcome as Kate's permission; hides that Kate asked her to stop

place: Calloway: the city archive
scene: The Aldous dyeworks' ink book shows one great order of Registry ink in the autumn of 646, the only one that year: one batch, one winter, the single ink of the relic rolls. The archive's index for the dyeworks lists half a dozen other entries, among them an infirmary book entry of 631, "a dyeworks hand, leg broken in a fall from the vats, discharged unhealed". She notes it because she notes everything, and moves on. Fen is in the archive too, nosing, and they have an edgy exchange about sources
what_changes: The relic rolls were written in one winter from one batch of ink; Fen has seen Tamsin in the archive
reader_knows_by_end: The relics' ink was one batch of 646; a dyeworks hand broke her leg in 631 (one entry among several)
pov_lens: Notices the ink book's columns, the index cards' typing, Fen's shoes; misreads the infirmary entry as irrelevant; hides from Fen what she is reading

place: Calloway: the Registry survey room
scene: Tamsin uses her pass to test the copies against older surveys. In the survey room she finds an old survey of the eastern smallholdings with a clerk's pencilled notes in the margins, citing earlier surveys by year and folio. She photographs them, as she photographs everything, and has not read them when Agnes comes in. Agnes does not shout. She reads Tamsin the terms of the pass, and says that a freelancer who casts doubt on the relic rolls in the anniversary year casts doubt on every title in Calloway. One more week to finish the orchard, then the pass is gone
what_changes: Agnes has set a deadline; Tamsin has photographs she has not read; her theory takes shape as she argues with Agnes
reader_knows_by_end: Margin notes exist in an old survey; Agnes's argument about title is a real one
pov_lens: Notices the survey's folds, pencil in the margin, Agnes's new glasses; misreads Agnes's fear for title as fear of her; hides what she has already photographed

place: Calloway: Kate's ward, nights
scene: A bad night. A woman with no family is dying, and Kate sits with her when she can. On her break there is a text from Aunt Ros saying how nice it was to see Tamsin. Kate does not reply to Tamsin. At the end of the shift she rings Juno instead and asks whether Tamsin has been lying to her too. Juno says Tamsin doesn't lie, she just doesn't say
what_changes: Kate knows Tamsin went behind her back; the friendship breaks; Kate and Juno draw closer
reader_knows_by_end: Tamsin has broken her promise; what the ward costs Kate; a woman dies with no one to read her name
pov_lens: Notices the patient's breathing, the clock, the other nurse's fatigue; misreads Juno's defence as taking sides; hides from Juno how hurt she is

place: Calloway: a café near the Order library, then the reading room
scene: Tamsin asks Perpetua for coffee and gives her the wrong answer. The relic rolls are copies, written in one winter in one ink by Senna, and Marit's diary says so; the copies won the eastern land back from the Teagues in 649; Dorcas, who kept them, became keeper; the Great Life borrowed a death. Senna and Dorcas forged the copies for the Order, and Senna was sent away to make it look like justice. It fits everything she has. Perpetua says it is the best case against the Cause she has heard and asks for it in writing. Tamsin writes it in the reading room that afternoon
what_changes: Tamsin has committed to the wrong answer and given it to the Examiner in writing
reader_knows_by_end: Tamsin's theory in full, and why it persuades
pov_lens: Notices Perpetua's hand round the cup, the clock, her own fluency; misreads Perpetua's interest as agreement; hides the margin notes she has not read

place: Calloway: the chapter house
scene: Perpetua files a preliminary report to the chapter as Examiner: the relic rolls are copies of a single winter; the Great Life's death is borrowed from Hild; "a researcher's hypothesis" that the copies were made in the Order's interest deserves inquiry. Hesketh reads it in front of her and says, quietly, that it is good work. Before the end of the day Agnes Mure asks the chapter's clerk for a copy
what_changes: The theory is now an official document; Hesketh is hurt; Agnes has the report
reader_knows_by_end: The preliminary report exists; Agnes will use it; Hesketh's grace
pov_lens: Notices Hesketh's silence, the clerk's stamp, her own pride; misreads her office as protection; hides that she named Tamsin as her source

place: Calloway: the Registry desk, then Linnet Street
scene: A letter from the Registry withdraws Tamsin's search pass for "a published hypothesis tending to impugn the titles of this city", a formula she once helped draft. She takes the pass back in person; the clerk at the desk will not look at her. At home Juno is at the piano with the concert proofs. The concert is on 8 April. Without turning round, Juno asks whether Tamsin will be there. Tamsin says yes
what_changes: Tamsin is shut out of the Registry; Juno asks again, in a smaller way
reader_knows_by_end: Agnes used the report; the concert is on the eve of the anniversary
pov_lens: Notices the letter's wording, the clerk's face, Juno's back; misreads Juno's question as only about the concert; hides that she is afraid she is wrong

place: Calloway: the porters' lodge and a steward's room
scene: Interlude: Bett Langley, Registry porter, present tense. Rent owing, her mother's chest, the porters' lodge stove. A woman from a great house sits her down in a back room, tells her what she saw, and counts coins onto the table. Bett buys shoes on the way home and does not look at them that night
what_changes: None: an interlude
reader_knows_by_end: A poor woman at the Registry is paid for a statement about what she saw
pov_lens: Never names the steward, her mistress, the accused or the charge; Bett does not think of herself as lying, only as agreeing

place: Calloway: Linnet Street
scene: Shut out, Tamsin goes through every photograph she has to write up the orchard. Among them are the survey-room margin notes. The hand is hurried and uncorrected, except once, where the clerk struck out her own mistake with the hooked stroke. The notes cite surveys of 590 and 612, and the copies follow them exactly, even where the Order lost land by it. Her theory fails on her own photograph. She rings Perpetua, gets no answer, and sits for an hour with the piano lid down
what_changes: The copies are honest; Tamsin's wrong answer is disproved by her own evidence, and it is already an official report
reader_knows_by_end: Senna's 645 notes; the copies match older surveys against the Order's interest; Tamsin was wrong
pov_lens: Notices the one stroke in the notes, the folio numbers, the dates; misreads her mistake as entirely her own fault; hides it from Juno for a day

place: Calloway: the Order archive
scene: Perpetua has read Tamsin's correction overnight. She takes Tamsin into the Order archive on the Examiner's warrant, which the Order cannot refuse and which she has never used for a guest. In the 647 tribunal register Perpetua knows the old formula when she sees it: "made dead to the Keeping" is a sentence, still on the books, almost never used. Bound in with it is the charge sheet: the evidence of forgery was the copies themselves, the rolls in the chapel window. She sends for the later sentences and finds a 690 petition from another woman made dead, asking to be restored. Then she has to decide what to do about her report
what_changes: Being "made dead" was a sentence, not a death; the relics were the trial exhibits; Perpetua's report is wrong in public
reader_knows_by_end: Senna was sentenced, not killed; the relics convicted her; the formula can be checked against other cases
pov_lens: Notices the register's formula, a clerk's hand of 647, the binding; misreads Tamsin's silence as triumph; hides her fear for her office

place: Wexham: the orchard at night
scene: A frost night. Bryony sits up with the burners in the rows at three in the morning, and Orla's car pulls into the lane: she has seen the forecast too. They work the rows together. Orla says the builder will walk if there is no answer by the end of April, and the Order has named a figure for the letters. Towards dawn Bryony tells her about the packet she held back from the box in December, tied with tape, which their mother told them never to read aloud. At first light Bryony rings Tamsin and says she can have it
what_changes: Bryony gives up the packet; the sisters have spent a night on the same side
reader_knows_by_end: The Order's figure; the builder's deadline; there are letters Tamsin has not seen; their mother kept them apart
pov_lens: Notices the thermometer, the tight buds, Orla's thin coat; misreads Orla's help as a tactic; hides from Orla that she has read the packet

place: Calloway: the city archive, the Teague deposit
scene: To find who bought the case, Tamsin asks for the Teague papers, open by appointment. Delphine is there, sorting family papers for a historical society talk she regrets agreeing to. In the steward's accounts for 647 they find "B. L., for her word", and Delphine reads B. as Benedicta: a household paying its own head for a statement, which makes a sort of sense. Tamsin shows her Perpetua's note of the tribunal witness: Bett Langley, porter. Then, among Benedicta's letters, a note to the keeper of the Registry: "the eastern entries, as we discussed." Delphine understands before Tamsin says it
what_changes: The witness was bought; Benedicta asked for the altered entries and then sat in judgment; Delphine knows
reader_knows_by_end: The Teague household bought a witness and commissioned the forgery; Delphine holds the proof; her family's grievance is false
pov_lens: Notices Delphine's gloves, the steward's columns, the note's fold; misreads Delphine's composure as indifference; hides that Fen has been asking about her

place: Wexham: the Rook kitchen
scene: In the kitchen where she first saw the bundle, Tamsin reads the packet: Dorcas Pryor's letter of 655, offering restoration if Senna will say the copies were forgeries, and Senna's fair copy of her refusal. Then she takes out the letter signed M. that she set aside in December and reads it properly: "The children are well. Wren has your hand. Do not write again." Bryony makes tea and asks who M. was. Tamsin knows and does not say
what_changes: Tamsin knows why Senna stayed dead, and that Marit knew where she was and chose silence; she now holds Kate's family's secret
reader_knows_by_end: Dorcas offered restoration for a confession and Senna refused; Senna was happier in Wexham and half admits it; Marit knew
pov_lens: Notices Dorcas's careful hand, Senna's stroke in her own fair copy, the M.; misreads Bryony's question as idle; hides Marit's name

place: Calloway: Kate's mother's house
scene: Kate's days off: her mother's shopping, the final proof of the order of service, and a call from Juno, who says Tamsin has found something she is frightened of, wants to tell Kate, and cannot. Kate says she does not want to know before the anniversary. Aunt Ros arrives with the family roll for the committee's photographer, who wants it for the souvenir booklet, and the three of them argue about whether the short reading would be easier on Ros's knees
what_changes: Kate refuses, by choice, to hear it before the anniversary; the Aldous roll is going into the souvenir booklet
reader_knows_by_end: Kate knows there is something; the Aldouses as a family; the anniversary is a week away
pov_lens: Notices her mother's swollen ankles, Ros's hands on the roll, the strain in Juno's voice; misreads the call as Tamsin using Juno; hides that she has guessed it is about Marit

place: Calloway: Hesketh's study at the Order's college
scene: Perpetua writes to the chapter withdrawing her preliminary report and takes the new evidence to Hesketh first, because thirty years require it. Hesketh reads the register and the charge sheet and believes them. She concedes the letters gracefully, since the meeting house's reading copies are centuries older than any Rook could have forged, and says the Cause is still not proved wrong: a woman unjustly sentenced who kept faith is still a saint. Delphine telephones while Perpetua is in the room and asks that the Cause's inquiries stay out of the Teague papers until after the housing vote. Hesketh says she will think about it. Then she tells Perpetua she will have her own expert examine the bones at the translation, to settle the tomb for good
what_changes: Perpetua has withdrawn her report; Hesketh will examine the bones; the deal with Delphine wobbles
reader_knows_by_end: Hesketh's case for the Cause even now; the translation on 9 April will include an examination; Delphine has asked for silence
pov_lens: Notices Hesketh's tablets, the phone cord, Delphine's voice through it; misreads Hesketh's calm as confidence; hides that she withdrew the report before telling her

place: Calloway: the Order archive
scene: On Perpetua's warrant Tamsin has one afternoon in the archive to check the 649 decree, "original by the grace of the Keeper", against the copies. Looking for Marit's name in the indexes, because the letter from M. will not leave her alone, she finds a petition of 655 filed under "Consolations of the bereaved": Marit asking to be released from a bond the sentence had already dissolved, "in case she is not dead to me". Photographs are forbidden here, so she copies it out by hand. She reads it as Marit making the break final
what_changes: Tamsin has Marit's petition and reads it as anger; the 649 decree is confirmed
reader_knows_by_end: The 649 decree made the copies originals by grace; Marit petitioned in 655; the archive filed it as consolation
pov_lens: Notices the catalogue's headings, the petition's corrections, the cold; misreads the petition as Marit closing the door; hides the copy from Perpetua

place: Wexham: the meeting house, a joint service
scene: The joint service the meeting house voted for: the Order's Wexham chapel and the Plain Keepers together, two days before the anniversary, with a long silence after the vote still in the room. Bryony reads one of the letters. Tamsin sits at the back beside Win Corley, who sings flat. Afterwards in the kitchen Bryony asks her plainly where Grandmother Senna is buried, then, because Orla has heard from Fen that Calloway will open the tomb on Saturday. Tamsin does not know. It is the first question she cannot answer from a document
what_changes: The tomb is the question now; Tamsin has no answer
reader_knows_by_end: The tomb will be opened at the translation on 9 April; if Senna lived, who is in it?
pov_lens: Notices the two congregations' coats, Win's hymnbook, Bryony's hands in the sink; misreads Bryony's question as a test; hides that she has no answer

place: Calloway: the Order archive
scene: Interlude: the cataloguer, present tense. A winter afternoon, a bundle of unsorted petitions, a colleague's cough, bread and cheese at the desk. A widow's petition to be released from a dead woman's bond: there can be only one reason a widow writes that, and she writes the heading, Consolations of the bereaved, and goes home in the dark
what_changes: None: an interlude
reader_knows_by_end: An archivist files a petition by the only reason she can imagine
pov_lens: Never names Marit or Senna; the cataloguer is not hiding anything and is not careless

place: Calloway: the Registry Chapel, the anniversary concert
scene: Juno's setting of the hymn is sung in public for the first time, Wallgate's four notes in it, the last verse rising. Tamsin is in the third row with Kate two seats away, not speaking. Afterwards in the vestry Juno, flushed, asks what Tamsin heard. Tamsin says it was beautiful. Juno says that is not what she asked
what_changes: The setting is out in the world; Juno knows Tamsin listened as a researcher; Kate and Tamsin have sat in one row
reader_knows_by_end: The anniversary begins; Juno's setting; Kate and Tamsin are estranged
pov_lens: Notices Juno's hands, Kate's ward shoes under her good coat, the relic cases dark behind the choir; misreads Juno's question as about the music; hides what the last line now means to her

place: Calloway: the Registry Chapel, the translation
scene: The 375th anniversary. Honor reads the death scene for the last time, both her lines in it. The tomb is opened for the translation of the bones to the new shrine, before the chapter, the council and the press. Behind a screen in a side chapel Hesketh's expert examines the bones before they are moved, as Hesketh promised. Perpetua, as Examiner, sees what is there: an older woman, a leg that healed badly. The expert tells Hesketh, quietly, that a hard life ages a skeleton. Fen is in the press seats, writing
what_changes: The bones look far older than thirty-one and have a badly healed leg; Hesketh has the opinion she wanted; Fen has seen the screen
reader_knows_by_end: The bones are a woman who looks about sixty with a badly healed break; the first expert's reading; the anniversary as Calloway keeps it
pov_lens: Notices the leg, Honor's two lines, Hesketh's hand on the screen; misreads the expert's confidence as competence; hides from Hesketh what she saw

place: Wexham: the Plain Keeping burial ground
scene: Pear blossom. Two days after the tomb was opened, Bryony decides it is time, and takes Tamsin, and Perpetua, who has come on the 22 with a folding stool, behind the meeting house to the stone the family has always tended: "Senna, schoolmistress, kept by those who knew her", 678. Orla comes too, uninvited, with flowers from the pharmacy bucket still in their cellophane. A saint with two graves. Bryony says she always knew where Grandmother Senna was; nobody asked
what_changes: Senna's real grave is found; the sisters stand at it together; Perpetua has seen it
reader_knows_by_end: Senna died in Wexham in 678 and is buried there; the Rooks descend from her Wexham household; so who is in the tomb?
pov_lens: Notices the blossom, moss in the letters, the cellophane; misreads Perpetua's silence as disapproval; hides how glad she is that Orla came

place: Calloway: the Courier's offices, then the river
scene: Fen's column: "The Saint Who Lived?", with the tribunal formula from Perpetua's withdrawn report, and a second expert at the university who disputes the age of the bones. Tamsin goes to the Courier to have it out with Fen and finds her less wrong than she would like: the second expert says a woman of about sixty, with a shin broken decades before her death and badly set. Walking home along the river past The Dyehouse flats, Tamsin remembers the infirmary entry from March
what_changes: The public knows the saint may have lived; the experts disagree; the infirmary entry is back in Tamsin's mind
reader_knows_by_end: Science disagrees with itself; the leg and the 631 entry may be one woman; Fen is often right, sloppily
pov_lens: Notices Fen's desk, the second report on her screen, the river; misreads Fen's glee as malice; hides the infirmary entry from Fen

place: Calloway: Aunt Ros's house, then Linnet Street
scene: After Fen's column the family gathers at Ros's without being asked. Kate reads the diary entry for 652, "word from W.", with the family listening for it for the first time. Ros says Marit was protecting the children; Kate says Marit lied to them for forty years; a cousin says both. Kate takes the diary to Linnet Street and gives it to Tamsin. Tamsin shows her the copy of Marit's petition. Kate reads "in case she is not dead to me" as hope, and says so, and says: find out what Marit knew, then tell me first
what_changes: The family knows Marit knew; the argument reopens on new ground; Kate gives Tamsin the diary and her terms
reader_knows_by_end: Marit knew Senna was alive and near; the petition can be read as hope as well as anger; Kate's terms
pov_lens: Notices who sits where, Ros's tea going cold, Tamsin's kitchen; misreads her own anger as about Tamsin; hides that she cried on the bus

place: Calloway: Linnet Street, the kitchen table
scene: Tamsin lays it out the way she used to lay out a title. The infirmary entry of 631: a dyeworks hand, the leg. Marit's diary, now hers to read: spoiled madder to the woman on the chapel porch, who knew the colour by the smell. The alms book in the chapel case, open at the edge of every photograph she took of the relic rolls in December: Jory of the porch, bread and a blanket, week after week, then nothing after a week in the spring of 647. And the translation record's phrase, on the tomb she has passed all her working life: the grave signed with her hand. Senna was in Wexham, and her stroke was on a grave in Calloway. Juno comes home and finds the kitchen covered
what_changes: The tomb holds Jory of the porch; Senna marked her grave; Tamsin knows the second layer
reader_knows_by_end: Jory worked at the Aldous dyeworks, broke her leg, lived on the chapel porch and died the week Senna left; the stroke on her grave was Senna's mark for a woman with no name anyone would write
pov_lens: Notices each document's date against the next, the gap in the alms book, Juno's keys in the door; misreads certainty as the end of it; hides nothing from Juno, for once, and finds she cannot explain it

place: Calloway: the chapter house and Hesketh's study
scene: Hesketh's expert's full report arrives, and so does the university's, which Hesketh commissioned herself to answer Fen. They disagree about the age and agree about the leg. Hesketh asks Perpetua for everything, and Perpetua gives her Tamsin's file on Jory. Hesketh reads it in her study and says she will tell the chapter that the Cause is withdrawn. Perpetua's own report, which she now has to write, will end her office. They have their Wednesday lunch on a Thursday
what_changes: Hesketh's own examination has condemned the Cause; she will withdraw it; Perpetua's office will end with her report
reader_knows_by_end: Documents, not the science, settle who is in the tomb; Hesketh's decision; what it costs Perpetua
pov_lens: Notices the two reports' margins, Hesketh's hand flat on the file, the wrong day for lunch; misreads Hesketh's acceptance as defeat; hides that she is relieved

place: Calloway: the city archive
scene: Tamsin goes back to the city archive as a reader like any other, to find Jory anywhere else. In the city fines for 639: "Jory, of no roll, for sleeping out by the Registry Chapel." Agnes is in the archive, which she never is, and sits down across the table. She has read Fen and the report, and says what she has always said: if the relics were trial exhibits, every title in Calloway rests on a forgery ruling, and someone will try it on. Tamsin says the copies are honest and better than what they replaced. Agnes says she knows
what_changes: Jory has a second record; Agnes and Tamsin agree the titles stand; Agnes will speak for the copies
reader_knows_by_end: Jory was fined in 639, of no roll; Agnes's fear is real and she is honest
pov_lens: Notices the fine book's clerk's hand, Agnes's tiredness, the archive clock; misreads Agnes's visit as a summons; hides that she has missed the Registry

place: Calloway: Linnet Street
scene: Tamsin tells Juno all of it, at the kitchen table, from the orchard to the porch. Then she asks what Juno thinks they should do about a woman nobody wrote down. Juno asks what Tamsin means to do. Tamsin does not know. Juno asks her own question again, and Tamsin, for the first time, does not say after this job. She does not say anything else either, and Juno goes up to bed
what_changes: Juno knows everything; Tamsin has stopped saying after this job; what to do about Jory is open
reader_knows_by_end: Juno's question is alive; Tamsin has no plan for Jory yet
pov_lens: Notices Juno's face, the score on the piano, the time; misreads Juno's silence as judgement; hides nothing

place: Calloway: Kate's flat
scene: Tamsin tells Kate first, before anyone official, because Kate is owed it: Senna lived, Marit knew, and the family has been kneeling at the grave of a woman Marit gave spoiled madder to. It breaks the Cause Kate worked for. Kate is quiet for a long time, then says that the hymn's last line was always about copying, and she supposes she knew. She will still answer kept at the Reading. She will read Senna's name with the dead, as Marit did, because Marit was right and wrong
what_changes: Kate knows everything; her faith survives, changed; the friendship survives on Kate's terms
reader_knows_by_end: Kate's faith after the truth; the hymn's last line read anew
pov_lens: Notices Kate's hands round the mug, the photograph of the Reading, the ward rota on the fridge; misreads Kate's quiet as the end of the friendship; hides how frightened she was to come

place: Calloway: the chapter house, then the Courier
scene: A special sitting. Hesketh withdraws the Cause in public, and gives her reasons, and they are good ones. Perpetua lays her final report before the chapter, and with it gives up the Examiner's office and the flat. In the gallery Delphine Teague listens; that evening the Courier carries her own statement about what Benedicta Teague did, before anyone else can publish it. Perpetua reads it at Hesketh's kitchen table, on a Monday, which is now their day
what_changes: The Cause is withdrawn; Perpetua has lost her office; Delphine has published her ancestor's guilt herself
reader_knows_by_end: The Order argues and does not fall; Delphine's choice and its cost; Hesketh and Perpetua go on
pov_lens: Notices the chapter's faces, Delphine's stillness, the boxes in her own flat; misreads Delphine's statement as calculation; hides from Hesketh that she has nowhere to live yet

place: Wexham: the orchard
scene: Thinning time. Tamsin's final report: the roll's line, Senna's corrected one, stands, and the pear row is split down the middle as it always legally was. Orla has sold the letters to the Order, for her daughter's fees, and has told the builder no. So the orchard stays an orchard, and the sisters will work the pear row between them. Thinning fruitlets side by side, they talk about their mother's funeral at last, badly
what_changes: The orchard is settled and not sold; the letters are the Order's; the sisters are speaking
reader_knows_by_end: The boundary on the corrected roll; Orla's sale of the letters; Bryony keeps the orchard
pov_lens: Notices the fruitlets, Orla's hands, Tamsin's report in a plastic sleeve; misreads Orla's sale as a betrayal, then not; hides that she cried at the funeral

place: Calloway: Hesketh's study
scene: Tamsin brings Hesketh Jory's life as she has assembled it: born on a barge and never written, a hand at the dyeworks, the leg in 631, the fine in 639, the porch, bread and a blanket, a grave Senna paid for. Hesketh offers her the keepership's pen to write Jory into the public roll at midsummer, on one condition: that she renew her oath, "I keep it twice, by Senna's rolls". Tamsin will not swear by the documents that made Senna dead. She says so, and knows whose refusal she is repeating
what_changes: Tamsin has refused the oath; Jory cannot go into the public roll by her hand
reader_knows_by_end: Jory's whole life as the records allow it; the oath and why Tamsin refuses it
pov_lens: Notices Hesketh's pen, the oath card's print, her own steadiness; misreads Hesketh's offer as a test; hides that she wanted to say yes

place: Calloway: the Infirmary, then Linnet Street
scene: On the ward radio: the housing vote has passed, narrowly. After her shift Kate goes to Linnet Street, where Tamsin and Juno want to take Jory in and have asked her how it is done, because Kate's family did it once, in 1890. Kate shows them, with Aunt Ros on speakerphone correcting her. Tamsin writes the name. Juno reads it. Kate answers kept
what_changes: Jory is written into Tamsin and Juno's household roll
reader_knows_by_end: Taking in, done; the housing vote has passed
pov_lens: Notices Juno's hand steady on the roll, Tamsin's cold one, Ros's voice; misreads nothing; hides that she has asked herself whether she would do it

place: Calloway: the Registry Chapel, then Linnet Street
scene: Midsummer chapter. The Order votes its decree: copies made in good faith keep. Its first act under it is to copy one entry from a household roll in Holm into the public roll, and the chapter's clerk does it at a table under the relic cases while Tamsin watches from the back with Agnes. Afterwards Tamsin walks home. The household roll is on the kitchen table where they left it, with Jory's name in it, and Juno has the pen. Below Jory's name they leave a space
what_changes: The Order's new decree; Jory is in the public roll by a copy; Juno's question is answered
reader_knows_by_end: The copy keeps; the space below Jory's name
pov_lens: Notices the clerk's hand copying hers, Agnes beside her, the roll on the table; misreads nothing she needs to; hides nothing
